hints.title: API Call Budget Obstacle
hints.text: Every call to isBadVersion incurs API latency. Since once a version is bad all subsequent versions are bad, how can you minimize queries to find the earliest fault?

hints.title: Monotonic Boolean Step Invariant
hints.text: The sequence of bad statuses is False, False, ..., True, True. The earliest True is the boundary where isBadVersion(mid) transitions.

hints.title: First Occurrence Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left = 1 and right = n. While left < right, let mid = left + (right - left) // 2. If isBadVersion(mid) is true, the first bad version is at or before mid (right = mid). Otherwise it is strictly after mid (left = mid + 1). Return left.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection issuing at most 32 API queries in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing versions sequentially takes O(N) API calls, exceeding query time limits on 2^31 versions.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using mid = left + (right - left) // 2 to avoid 32-bit signed integer overflow.
